properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 13 at 8:12PM MST until September 13 at 9:45PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
At 812 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 0.7 and 1.2 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Douglas and Pirtleville.

This includes the following highways...
Route 80 between mile markers 363 and 370. Route 191 between mile
markers 1 and 3.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 945 PM MST THIS EVENING FOR SOUTHEASTERN COCHISE COUNTY

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 13 at 6:25PM MST until September 13 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 625 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain over the Havasu Creek basin. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
A stream gage on Cataract Creek below Topocoba Gorge near Supai
recorded around a 5.0 foot rise at 6:00 PM MST.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Havasu Creek basin.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Havasu Creek basin.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Little Navajo Falls, Mooney Falls, Beaver Falls, Hualapai Hilltop,
Havasupai Reservation and Supai.

This includes the Colorado River between river miles 156 and 158.

This includes the following swimming holes...
All swimming holes on Havasu Creek near Supai.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Colorado River, Sinyella Canyon, Heather Wash, Pasture Wash, Little
Coyote Canyon, Havasu Creek and Black Tank Wash.
properties.instruction:
Campers and hikers should hustle to higher ground immediately! Stay
away from creeks and washes!

Foot bridges will be washed out in Supai Campground. Some campsites
will be flooded. Campers may be stranded in portions of the
campground.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 13 at 8:25PM MDT until September 13 at 11:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Lee burn scar in...
South Central Rio Blanco County in northwestern Colorado...

* Until 1130 PM MDT.

* At 825 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Lee Burn Scar. Between 0.3 and 0.5 inches of
rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 2 to 4 inches in 1
hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other
loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Lee Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Lee Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of South Central Rio Blanco County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Lee Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:30 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:30 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 13 at 9:28PM MDT until September 13 at 10:15PM MDT by NWS Great Falls MT
properties.description:
SVRTFX

The National Weather Service in Great Falls has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Judith Basin County in central Montana...
South central Chouteau County in north central Montana...

* Until 1015 PM MDT.

* At 928 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 12 miles southwest
of Geyser, or 24 miles west of Stanford, moving northeast at 35
mph.

HAZARD...Quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Damage to vehicles is expected.

* Locations impacted include...
Geyser and Raynesford.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 13 at 9:30PM MDT until September 13 at 9:45PM MDT by NWS Great Falls MT
properties.description:
At 930 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 22 miles northwest
of Winifred, or 34 miles southeast of Big Sandy, moving northeast at
35 mph.

HAZARD...Quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Damage to vehicles is expected.

Locations impacted include...
Judith Landing and Iliad.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 13 at 7:09PM EDT until September 14 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Norton has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Rhode Island...

Pawtuxet River At Cranston affecting Kent and Providence Counties.

For the Pawtuxet River...including Cranston, Scituate Reservoir...
Minor flooding is forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 200 AM EDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pawtuxet River at Cranston.

* WHEN...From this evening to late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding will occur along the
river as it flows through Warwick and Cranston.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:45 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 9.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.1 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage just after
midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.1
feet on 11/06/1955.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
